title: Affine pushforward is perverse up to the relative dimension
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring whose additive exponent is invertible in $k$. Let $a_Y:Y	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a separated morphism of finite type, let $f:X	o Y$ be an affine morphism of finite type [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], put $a_X=a_Yf$, and let $d\ge0$ be an integer such that every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y=X	imes_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$, $y\in Y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], has topological Krull dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Work in the ordinary derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ of the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with the compact-support direct image $Rf_!$ of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] (compactifications exist by [thm-nagata-compactification]), the right adjoints $a_T^	imes$ of $Ra_{T!}$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], $\omega_T=a_T^	imes\Lambda$ and $D_T=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,\omega_T)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] for $T=X,Y$. Let $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be the bounded constructible complexes [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] of finite Tor amplitude. Read the support condition and the perverse classes of [def-per-support-condition, def-per-perverse-subcategories] at these finite coefficients: $\operatorname{SuppCon}(K)$ means that for every $i\in\mathbf Z$ the closed support of a sheaf (the complement of the largest Zariski open on which it vanishes; by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] this is the closure of the set of points with a nonzero geometric stalk) of $\mathcal H^{-i}K$ has dimension at most $i$, the empty set having dimension $-\infty$; $K\in{}^pD^{\le n}(T)$ means $\operatorname{SuppCon}(K[n])$, and $K\in{}^pD^{\ge n}(T)$ means $\operatorname{SuppCon}(D_T(K[n]))$. Then for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ and every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$

$$K\in{}^pD^{\le n}(X)\ \Longrightarrow\ Rf_!K\in{}^pD^{\le n+d}(Y),\qquad K\in{}^pD^{\ge n}(X)\ \Longrightarrow\ Rf_!K\in{}^pD^{\ge n-d}(Y).$$

The instance used by the Fourier transform is $d=1$, for the projection $p_2:\mathbf A^1_{k_0}	imes\mathbf A^1_{k_0}	o\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ and its base changes. These are the upstream declarations isPerverseLE_lowerShriek and isPerverseGE_lowerShriek (finite coefficients $\Lambda$, any field $k$, $K$ of finite Tor amplitude).

proof.text: Three formal facts are used throughout. (a) On a compactification $f=rj$, $Rf_!=Rr_*Dj_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Extension by zero is exact [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], so its termwise derived functor is triangulated [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; $Rr_*$ is triangulated on the unbounded categories by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Their composite is triangulated [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite], hence commutes with shifts. Also $D_T(M[m])\cong D_T(M)[-m]$ by [lem-pur-derived-internal-hom-shift-left]. (b) If $\operatorname{SuppCon}(M)$ and $e\ge0$, then $\operatorname{SuppCon}(M[e])$: $\mathcal H^{-i}(M[e])=\mathcal H^{-(i-e)}(M)$ has closed support of dimension at most $i-e\le i$. (c) The support condition is extension closed. The cohomology sequence of a distinguished triangle $M'\to M\to M''\to M'[1]$ for the standard t-structure, whose cohomology objects are the cohomology sheaves [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category, lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] shows that $\mathcal H^{-i}M$ vanishes wherever both outer sheaves vanish. Its closed support is therefore contained in their union. An irreducible closed subset of a union of two closed subsets lies in one of them, so every chain of irreducible closed subsets lies in the member containing its largest term; the dimension of that union is the maximum of the two dimensions. This proves (c), including empty supports.

source.place: Tag 05SE (proposition-derived-functor), Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), Tag 014Y (lemma-composition-exact); the support and dimension calculation is written out

proof.text: Support side. Let $K\in{}^pD^{\le n}(X)\cap D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and put $K'=K[n]$, so $\operatorname{SuppCon}(K')$ holds and $K'$ is bounded with constructible cohomology sheaves $F_i=\mathcal H^{-i}K'$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The closed support of $F_i$ has dimension at most $i$; in particular $F_i=0$ for $i<0$. By (a) the claim $Rf_!K\in{}^pD^{\le n+d}(Y)$ is $\operatorname{SuppCon}((Rf_!K')[d])$. For a bounded complex, successive truncation triangles have cohomology-sheaf quotients $F_i[i]$. Thus the truncation triangles of the standard t-structure on $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category, lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] build $K'$ from the finitely many objects $F_i[i]$ by extensions. Since $Rf_!$ is exact, (c) reduces the claim to $\operatorname{SuppCon}((Rf_!F_i)[i+d])$ for each $i\ge0$. Now $\mathcal H^{-m}((Rf_!F_i)[i+d])=R^{q}f_!F_i$ with $q=i+d-m$, and [lem-per-finite-compact-support-fibre-support-bound], applied with $a=i$, bounds the dimension of its closed support by $i+d-q=m$. This is the support condition.

source.place: 4.2.4 and the fibre dimension count behind 4.1.1; fibres of an affine morphism of relative dimension d

proof.text: Exchange. For every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ there is a natural isomorphism $D_YRf_!M\cong Rf_*D_XM$. Indeed the composition isomorphism $Ra_{Y!}Rf_!\cong Ra_{X!}$ [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] gives, by uniqueness of right adjoints [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], $f^\times a_Y^\times\cong a_X^\times$, hence $\omega_X\cong f^\times\omega_Y$. The internal adjunction [prop-asd-internal-adjunction], applied with $K=\omega_Y$, is $Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(M,f^\times\omega_Y)\cong R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(Rf_!M,\omega_Y)$. All schemes are of finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian, and $f$, $a_Y$, $a_X$ are compactifiable by [thm-nagata-compactification]. No finiteness theorem and no biduality is used here.

source.place: 4.1.2 (duality exchanges Rf_! and Rf_*); the ordinary etale form of the exchange D_Y Rf_! = Rf_* D_X

proof.text: Cosupport side. Let $K\in{}^pD^{\ge n}(X)\cap D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and put $L=D_X(K[n])$, so $\operatorname{SuppCon}(L)$ holds by definition. By [lem-per-finite-coefficient-dual-constructible], applied to the bounded constructible complex $K[n]$, $L$ lies in $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and has constructible cohomology sheaves. Since $f$ is affine, [lem-per-finite-affine-direct-image-support-bound] gives $\operatorname{SuppCon}(Rf_*L)$ for the bounded-below direct image. It agrees on $L$ with the unbounded $Rf_*$ of Step 3: a bounded-below injective resolution of $L$ is K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], and K-injective complexes compute the total derived functor [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. By the exchange of Step 3 and (a), $D_Y((Rf_!K)\lbrack n-d\rbrack)\cong D_Y(Rf_!(K[n]))[d]\cong(Rf_*L)[d]$, which satisfies the support condition by (b), as $d\ge0$. Hence $Rf_!K\in{}^pD^{\ge n-d}(Y)$. The argument gives the stronger affine bound $Rf_!K\in{}^pD^{\ge n}(Y)$ (the case $d=0$ of (b)).

source.place: Theorem 4.1.1 (Artin's affine estimate for Rf_*) and Corollary 4.1.2

proof.text: Both implications hold for every $n$, which is the statement. If $X$ is empty, $Rf_!K=0$ lies in every class. For the projection $p_2:\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\times\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\to\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, and after a base change $Y'\to\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, the inverse image of an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of the base is $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]$. Thus the map is affine and of finite type [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Its fibre over $y$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)[t]$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Euclidean division makes every nonzero prime of this polynomial ring maximal, and $(0)\subsetneq(t)$ is a chain of primes; its spectrum has dimension one. Consequently $d=1$ applies whenever the base $Y'$ is separated of finite type over $k_0$, as required by the theorem.
